description: Catalog of public datasets supported by umimic.data.public_datasets. Observation tables live as compressed long-form products (*_umimic.csv.xz); this file holds metadata only. Each entry records a DOI (where one exists), the preferred citation, and licence/redistribution notes for the derived product.

tshs_tumor.title: TSHS xenograft tumor growth
tshs_tumor.citation: Daskalakis C. Tumor Growth Dataset. TSHS Resources Portal, 2016. Available at https://www.causeweb.org/tshs/tumor-growth/.
tshs_tumor.license_notes: Permission granted for research use with citation of the source above. No additional conditions. No DOI is issued for this teaching dataset.

data_quality.summary: Based on a real experiment; some measurements were tweaked for teaching. Timing is irregular (typically every 2–3 days). Caliper volumes are error-prone.

flags.nonmonotonic_red: Red font in Excel: modest non-monotonic wiggle; normal measurement error — retained.
flags.suspicious_green: Green fill in Excel: larger fluctuation, possibly real late shrinkage — retained by default.
flags.exclude_clear_error: Orange fill in Excel: clearly wrong — removed from the distributed product (see EXCLUDED_VALUES.csv).

excluded_values.reason: Orange highlight; clearly wrong given preceding/following sizes.

phenopop.title: PhenoPop Ba/F3 live-cell imaging under imatinib
phenopop.citation: Wu C, Gunnarsson E, Myklebust EM, Kohn-Luque A, et al. Using birth-death processes to infer tumor subpopulation structure from live-cell imaging drug screening data. PLOS Computational Biology 20(3):e1011888, 2024. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011888
phenopop.license_notes: PLOS Computational Biology is open access under CC BY 4.0. Source data and MATLAB code at https://github.com/chenyuwu233/PhenoPop_stochastic. Redistribution with attribution is permitted.
phenopop.reference_notes: The authors' own published fits are shipped alongside the data: 72 fit rows and 81 bootstrap intervals covering the four mixtures (BF_11/12/21/41) and the monoclonal controls, for three models -- 'sto' (stochastic birth-death, the paper's contribution), 'dyn' (deterministic mean) and 'hl' (the original PhenoPop Hill deconvolution). This makes a head-to-head possible without re-running their MATLAB. Only element 0 of the birth-death parameter vectors is interpreted (the mixture proportion p), confirmed against the published ci_*_p intervals; the rest is preserved verbatim as JSON. Caution: estimated proportions do not match nominal seeding ratios (BF_11 is nominally 1:1, estimated ~0.30) -- that is the authors' published result, so nominal_ratio records the intended design, not ground truth.

hafner_gr.title: Hafner/Niepel GR metrics (breast cancer lines × drugs)
hafner_gr.citation: Hafner M, Niepel M, Subramanian K, Sorger PK. Quantification of sensitivity and resistance of breast cancer cell lines to anti-cancer drugs using GR metrics. Scientific Data 4:170166, 2017. doi:10.1038/sdata.2017.166. Data: Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.03n60
hafner_gr.license_notes: Scientific Data article CC BY 4.0; Dryad deposit released under CC0. Redistribution permitted with attribution.

nci60.title: NCI-60 DTP growth inhibition (endpoint screening)
nci60.citation: NCI Developmental Therapeutics Program (DTP). NCI-60 Growth Inhibition (GI) screening data. https://dtp.cancer.gov/databases_tools/bulk_data.htm
nci60.notes: Endpoint GI%/PTC screening (~2.5M rows). Prefer filters nsc= and/or cell_line=. Default representation reconstructs a 2-point count series from percent_of_control with nominal N0=10000 and assay_hours=48; use representation=endpoint_metrics for honest single-time GI%/PTC storage.
nci60.license_notes: US Government public-domain data produced by the NCI DTP. Free to use and redistribute; citation of DTP requested.

bestdr.title: BESTDR HCT116 + cisplatin live-cell imaging counts
bestdr.citation: McDonald TO, Bruno S, Roney JP, Zervantonakis IK, et al. BESTDR Enables Bayesian Quantification of Mechanism-Specific Drug Responses. Cancer Research, 2025. doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-1181
bestdr.notes: Compact extract: HCT116 cisplatin multi-well multi-FOV live/dead counts every 4 h (replicates + dose-response plates). Negative live counts clipped to 0 and flagged. Full multi-line BESTDR R data not vendored.
bestdr.license_notes: Article open access under CC BY-NC-ND via Europe PMC. Derived product redistributed for non-commercial research use with attribution. Preprint: bioRxiv 2025.02.05.636681.

whiting2025_barcode.title: Whiting 2025 bulk barcode population sizes (tiny extract)
whiting2025_barcode.citation: Whiting FJH, Mossner M, Gabbutt C, Kimberley C, et al. Quantitative measurement of phenotype dynamics during cancer drug resistance evolution using genetic barcoding. Nature Communications 16, 2025. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-59479-7
whiting2025_barcode.notes: Bulk population size vs time only (HCTbc / SW6bc, 4 replicates each). Not imaging. Not scRNA. Not full barcode matrices. Time in hours = day*24. Concentration=0 (pulsed treatment schedule).
whiting2025_barcode.license_notes: Nature Communications is open access under CC BY 4.0. Supplementary Data and Source Data files are redistributable with attribution.
whiting2025_barcode.lineage_notes: Long-form per-barcode abundances from Supplementary Data 2 (HCTbc_Barcode_Data, SW6bc_Barcode_Data): 5,619,208 rows covering 13,962 HCT116 and 688,439 SW620 barcodes across 4 sequencing timepoints x 2 plates. Zero counts are retained deliberately -- an absent barcode is an observed extinction, not a missing measurement. Library sizes differ between samples, so compare relative frequencies rather than raw counts. Column sums were verified against the source workbook.

csc_dip.title: Cancer stem cells / drug-induced plasticity (Wu et al. 2025)
csc_dip.citation: Wu C, Gunnarsson E, Foo J, Leder K. A statistical framework for detecting therapy-induced resistance from drug screens. npj Systems Biology and Applications, 2025. doi:10.1038/s41540-025-00560-8
csc_dip.license_notes: Article open access under CC BY-NC-ND via Europe PMC. No derived product is shipped because the underlying measurements are not available -- see availability below.
csc_dip.availability_notes: The public code repository contains the analysis scripts and the authors' stored results, but NOT the measurements they were run on. Every data input is loaded from a file absent from the repository, so no product can be built from it. Missing inputs: 'COLO858 data.xlsx', 'CPX paper (Figures 1E, 1F, 2A and 2B data).xlsx', 'CPX paper (Figures 1E and 2B data).xlsx' (readcell sources); DATA_COLO858_60h.mat, Forward_D24_v.mat, T12_2T_v.mat, rate24.mat (load sources). Only the Conc and Time vectors are inline in the scripts. Their published AIC/AICc values ARE extracted and shipped (16 rows: AGS gastric with CPX-O, its time-delay variant, and COLO858 with vemurafenib), so their model-selection conclusions remain comparable. Obtain the workbooks from the authors or the npj supplementary material before attempting a comparison.
experiments: AGS gastric line with CPX-O (Conc 0-16, Time 0/12/36 h, 2 replicates)
COLO858 melanoma line with vemurafenib (60 h)
csc_dip.results_available: Their published AIC values ship in the repository (In_vitro_AGS_AIC.mat, In_vitro_COLO858_60h_AIC.mat), so their conclusions can be compared even where their fit cannot be rerun.
